subject: science
description: Compare the observations made by different groups using the same tools.

subject: science

subject: science

subject: science

subject: science

subject: science
description: State the importance of preparing for severe weather, lightning, and other weather related events.

subject: science
description: Identify objects and materials as solid, liquid, or gas.

subject: science
description: Observe and describe water in its solid, liquid, and gaseous states.

subject: science
description: Measure and compare temperatures taken every day at the same time.

subject: science
description: Measure and compare the volume of liquids using containers of various shapes and sizes.

subject: science
description: Investigate that materials can be altered to change some of their properties, but not all materials respond the same way to any one alteration.

subject: science

subject: science
description: Investigate the effect of applying various pushes and pulls on different objects.

subject: science
description: Demonstrate that magnets can be used to make some things move without touching them.

subject: science
description: Recognize that objects are pulled toward the ground unless something holds them up.

subject: science
description: Demonstrate that the greater the force (push or pull) applied to an object, the greater the change in motion of the object.

subject: science
description: Distinguish human body parts (brain, heart, lungs, stomach, muscles, and skeleton) and their basic functions.

subject: science
description: Observe and describe major stages in the life cycles of plants and animals, including beans and butterflies.

subject: science
description: Compare and contrast the basic needs that all living things, including humans, have for survival.

subject: science
description: Recognize and explain that living things are found all over Earth, but each is only able to live in habitats that meet its basic needs.

subject: science
description: Compare the observations made by different groups using the same tools and seek reasons to explain the differences across groups.

subject: science
description: Keep records as appropriate, such as pictorial, written, or simple charts and graphs, of investigations conducted.

subject: science
description: Recognize the importance of communication among scientists.

subject: science
description: Recognize that scientists question, discuss, and check each other's evidence and explanations.

subject: science
description: Infer based on observation.

subject: science
description: Explain that empirical evidence is information, such as observations or measurements, that is used to help validate explanations of natural phenomena.

subject: science
description: Recognize that words in science can have different or more specific meanings than their use in everyday language; for example, energy, cell, heat/cold, and evidence.

subject: science
description: Recognize that scientists use models to help understand and explain how things work.

subject: science
description: Recognize that all models are approximations of natural phenomena; as such, they do not perfectly account for all observations.

subject: science

subject: science
description: Identify the Sun as a star that emits energy; some of it in the form of light.

subject: science
description: Recognize that the Sun appears large and bright because it is the closest star to Earth.

subject: science
description: Explore the Law of Gravity by demonstrating that gravity is a force that can be overcome.

subject: science
description: Investigate that the number of stars that can be seen through telescopes is dramatically greater than those seen by the unaided eye.

subject: science
description: Demonstrate that radiant energy from the Sun can heat objects and when the Sun is not present, heat may be lost.

subject: science
description: Measure and compare temperatures of various samples of solids and liquids.

subject: science
description: Measure and compare the mass and volume of solids and liquids.

subject: science
description: Compare materials and objects according to properties such as size, shape, color, texture, and hardness.

subject: science
description: Describe the changes water undergoes when it changes state through heating and cooling by using familiar scientific terms such as melting, freezing, boiling, evaporation, and condensation.

subject: science
description: Identify some basic forms of energy such as light, heat, sound, electrical, and mechanical.

subject: science
description: Recognize that energy has the ability to cause motion or create change.

subject: science
description: Demonstrate that light travels in a straight line until it strikes an object or travels from one medium to another.

subject: science
description: Demonstrate that light can be reflected, refracted, and absorbed.

subject: science
description: Investigate, observe, and explain that things that give off light often also give off heat.

subject: science
description: Investigate, observe, and explain that heat is produced when one object rubs against another, such as rubbing one's hands together.

subject: science
description: Describe structures in plants and their roles in food production, support, water and nutrient transport, and reproduction.

subject: science

subject: science

subject: science
description: Classify flowering and nonflowering plants into major groups such as those that produce seeds, or those like ferns and mosses that produce spores, according to their physical characteristics.

subject: science
description: Describe how animals and plants respond to changing seasons.

subject: science
description: Recognize that plants use energy from the Sun, air, and water to make their own food.

subject: science

subject: science
description: Compare the observations made by different groups using multiple tools and seek reasons to explain the differences across groups.

subject: science
description: Explain that science does not always follow a rigidly defined method ("the scientific method") but that science does involve the use of observations and empirical evidence.

subject: science
description: Attempt reasonable answers to scientific questions and cite evidence in support.

subject: science
description: Compare the methods and results of investigations done by other classmates.

subject: science
description: Keep records that describe observations made, carefully distinguishing actual observations from ideas and inferences about the observations.

subject: science
description: Recognize and explain that scientists base their explanations on evidence.

subject: science
description: Recognize that science involves creativity in designing experiments.

subject: science
description: Explain that science focuses solely on the natural world.

subject: science
description: Explain that models can be three dimensional, two dimensional, an explanation in your mind, or a computer model.

subject: science

subject: science
description: Describe the changes in the observable shape of the moon over the course of about a month.

subject: science
description: Recognize that Earth revolves around the Sun in a year and rotates on its axis in a 24-hour day.

subject: science
description: Relate that the rotation of Earth (day and night) and apparent movements of the Sun, Moon, and stars are connected.

subject: science
description: Investigate and report the effects of space research and exploration on the economy and culture of Florida.

subject: science

subject: science
description: Identify the physical properties of common earth-forming minerals, including hardness, color, luster, cleavage, and streak color, and recognize the role of minerals in the formation of rocks.

subject: science
description: Recognize that humans need resources found on Earth and that these are either renewable or nonrenewable.

subject: science
description: Describe the basic differences between physical weathering (breaking down of rock by wind, water, ice, temperature change, and plants) and erosion (movement of rock by gravity, wind, water, and ice).

subject: science
description: Investigate how technology and tools help to extend the ability of humans to observe very small things and very large things.

subject: science
description: Identify resources available in Florida (water, phosphate, oil, limestone, silicon, wind, and solar energy).

subject: science
description: Measure and compare objects and materials based on their physical properties including: mass, shape, volume, color, hardness, texture, odor, taste, attraction to magnets.

subject: science
description: Identify properties and common uses of water in each of its states.

subject: science

subject: science
description: Investigate and describe that magnets can attract magnetic materials and attract and repel other magnets.

subject: science
description: Identify some familiar changes in materials that result in other materials with different characteristics, such as decaying animal or plant matter, burning, rusting, and cooking.

subject: science
description: Observe and describe some basic forms of energy, including light, heat, sound, electrical, and the energy of motion.

subject: science
description: Investigate and describe that energy has the ability to cause motion or create change.

subject: science

subject: science
description: Describe how moving water and air are sources of energy and can be used to move things.

subject: science
description: Recognize that heat flows from a hot object to a cold object and that heat flow may cause materials to change temperature.

subject: science
description: Identify common materials that conduct heat well or poorly.

subject: science
description: Recognize that an object in motion always changes its position and may change its direction.

subject: science
description: Investigate and describe that the speed of an object is determined by the distance it travels in a unit of time and that objects can move at different speeds.

subject: science
description: Identify processes of sexual reproduction in flowering plants, including pollination, fertilization (seed production), seed dispersal, and germination.

subject: science
description: Explain that although characteristics of plants and animals are inherited, some characteristics can be affected by the environment.

subject: science
description: Recognize that animal behaviors may be shaped by heredity and learning.

subject: science

subject: science
description: Compare the seasonal changes in Florida plants and animals to those in other regions of the country.

subject: science
description: Explain that animals, including humans, cannot make their own food and that when animals eat plants or other animals, the energy stored in the food source is passed to them.

subject: science
description: Trace the flow of energy from the Sun as it is transferred along the food chain through the producers to the consumers.

subject: science
description: Recognize ways plants and animals, including humans, can impact the environment.

subject: science

description: Explain the difference between an experiment and other types of scientific investigation.

subject: science
description: Recognize and explain the need for repeated experimental trials.

subject: science
description: Identify a control group and explain its importance in an experiment.

subject: science
description: Recognize and explain that authentic scientific investigation frequently does not parallel the steps of "the scientific method."

subject: science
description: Recognize and explain the difference between personal opinion/interpretation and verified observation.

subject: science
description: Recognize and explain that science is grounded in empirical observations that are testable; explanation must always be linked with evidence.

subject: science
description: Recognize and explain that when scientific investigations are carried out, the evidence produced by those investigations should be replicable by others.

subject: science

subject: science

subject: science

subject: science

subject: science

subject: science
description: Investigate and describe some basic forms of energy, including light, heat, sound, electrical, chemical, and mechanical.

description: Identify and classify materials that conduct electricity and materials that do not.

subject: science

subject: science

subject: science

subject: science

subject: science
description: Analyze the methods used to develop a scientific explanation as seen in different fields of science.

subject: science

subject: science
description: Discuss what characterizes science and its methods.

subject: science

subject: science

subject: science
description: Summarize the effects of space exploration on the economy and culture of Florida.

subject: science
description: Explore the scientific theory of atoms (also known as atomic theory) by using models to explain the motion of particles in solids, liquids, and gases.

subject: science

subject: science
description: Explore and describe the densities of various materials through measurement of their masses and volumes.

subject: science
description: Classify and compare substances on the basis of characteristic physical properties that can be demonstrated or measured; for example, density, thermal or electrical conductivity, solubility, magnetic properties, melting and boiling points, and know that these properties are independent of the amount of the sample.

subject: science
description: Recognize that there are a finite number of elements and that their atoms combine in a multitude of ways to produce compounds that make up all of the living and nonliving things that we encounter.

subject: science
description: Recognize that elements are grouped in the periodic table according to similarities of their properties.

subject: science
description: Explore the scientific theory of atoms (also known as atomic theory) by recognizing that atoms are the smallest unit of an element and are composed of sub-atomic particles (electrons surrounding a nucleus containing protons and neutrons).

subject: science
description: Identify basic examples of and compare and classify the properties of compounds, including acids, bases, and salts.

subject: science
description: Distinguish among mixtures (including solutions) and pure substances.

subject: science
description: Explore the Law of Conservation of Mass by demonstrating and concluding that mass is conserved when substances undergo physical and chemical changes.

subject: science
description: Differentiate between physical changes and chemical changes.

subject: science
description: Investigate and describe how temperature influences chemical changes.

subject: science
description: Describe and investigate the process of photosynthesis, such as the roles of light, carbon dioxide, water and chlorophyll; production of food; release of oxygen.

subject: science
description: Describe and investigate how cellular respiration breaks down food to provide energy and releases carbon dioxide.

subject: science
description: Construct a scientific model of the carbon cycle to show how matter and energy are continuously transferred within and between organisms and their physical environment.

subject: science
description: Cite evidence that living systems follow the Laws of Conservation of Mass and Energy.
